whereItStands.value: The map follows a scholarship service from learning about it through project development, application, recommendation, review, award decision, enrollment, class participation, project work, presentation, and reporting outcomes. It spans several systems, including ClickUp, Teams, KualiBuild, Zoom, websites, email, newsletters, Excel, and the DES program manager’s registration process. Effort is concentrated around developing and evaluating projects, coordinating the evaluation committee, and supporting awardees as they take the class and work on their projects.

frictionPatterns.value: Friction clusters around evaluation coordination, use of available awardee support, and project impact validation. Committee coordination is moderate and frequent, involving repeated email exchanges about participants, dates, times, and calendar blocks. Low uptake of OSI support is moderate and occasional and is felt by awardees and the service team. Difficulty measuring or validating financial impact is high and frequent and is felt by candidates who lack the calculation knowledge or data needed for their projects.

decisionsForDesign.value: The design phase will weigh where the project task sits in relation to project acceptance (D-01), how applicants and submissions are reviewed and scored (D-02), how many scholarships can be awarded (D-03), and how recommendations on applications are given (D-04). These decisions include judgment-based decisions about project acceptance, scholarship capacity, and recommendations, alongside the clear-cut decision to review and score submissions.

openQuestions.value: The map does not specify the service scope, moments that matter, dropout points, or a friction summary in the lead’s words. It does not establish why many awardees do not take up OSI support, what data or calculation capability candidates have or lack in particular cases, or how evaluation committee coordination connects to the other stages. The map also leaves unsettled how the listed systems relate to each stage and decision.
